$comment: App-declared environment variables. Declare every variable this app reads beyond the platform-owned set; the Terp Studio deploy pipeline renders exactly the declared keys into a per-environment .app.env (see docker-compose.prod.yml), and `cp .app.env.example .app.env` exercises the same seam locally. Names match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$. Mark write-only secrets with "format": "secret" — their values are sealed, never stored in plain records. A field this dialect does not have is REFUSED, because the deploy side drops what it does not recognise: "secret": true is the plausible mistake and it is not the field — it is dropped, and the value is then stored in plain records rather than sealed. format is one of secret | port | hostname | plain. requiredIn names where a value must be set: a non-empty list of ENVIRONMENT values (local | staging | production). "required" means every environment, so a name is in one or the other, never both; a value only a deployment needs — JOB_SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID is the canonical case — is declared "requiredIn": ["production"]. A variable whose last word is SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, PASSPHRASE, KEY, CREDENTIAL or CREDENTIALS must declare one: "format": "secret" to seal it, or "format": "plain" to record that it holds no credential. Platform-owned names (SECRET_KEY, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, DATABASE_URL, ENVIRONMENT, WEB_PORT, BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS) are refused here. LIMITS, and the reader fails closed on the WHOLE file past any of them: at most 50 variables; type/title/description/format/group/resolvedBy are strings of at most 500 characters each; enum is at most 50 strings of at most 200 characters. Keep a description to a sentence or two — an explanation long enough to be complete is easily past the cap, and it would cost the app every declaration in this file. A declared variable must NOT also appear in a compose `environment:` block: compose resolves `environment:` over `env_file:`, so the declaration would be dead — `terp verify --only env-seams` fails on that overlap. For an address, set "resolvedBy" to who resolves it, because it cannot be inferred from the name or type: "container" (a service on the compose network dials it — use the service name, http://api:8000), "host" (your shell dials it — http://127.0.0.1:8000), or "browser" (the user's browser is sent there — a host address). See `terp guide environment`.

SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS.title: Previous signing keys (verify only)
SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS.description: Earlier SECRET_KEY values, comma-separated. They only verify sessions signed before a key rotation, each for its own lifetime, and never sign. Empty outside a rotation; drop once the longest session lifetime has passed (ADR 0189).

SECRET_KEY_DECRYPT_FALLBACKS.title: Previous sealing keys (decrypt only)
SECRET_KEY_DECRYPT_FALLBACKS.description: Earlier SECRET_KEY values, comma-separated. They only decrypt values sealed at rest before a key rotation, and never seal. Empty outside a rotation; drop once `terp secrets reseal` reports nothing left under them (ADR 0189).
